title: CR-016 The Ferry Across Unpainted Water
description: Original Southern Song-informed Chinese ink landscape as a vertical hanging-scroll painting on silk. Uses new_generation + EraPack song + ArtMethod chinese_ink_painting + artifact form scroll + newly_created. No TransformationPack, no reference images, no StylePack, no APCC. Painting-as-principal-image in a 4:5 field; historically_informed (not reconstruction of a named masterpiece). See docs/CR_016_FERRY_UNPAINTED_WATER.md. Creative Research library entry only; no gallery image attached.

semantic_spec.request: Create an original historically informed Southern Song Chinese ink landscape as a vertical hanging-scroll painting on silk. The painting itself is the principal image filling a 4:5 field—not a studio photograph of a mounted scroll object, not a living photographic scene, not a timber-corridor fashion editorial, and not a fashion-portrait afterimage. Compose one continuous quiet river crossing with coherent hanging-scroll hierarchy: upper mist-softened distant hills in sparse high-value washes; middle broad river space with substantial reserved unpainted silk and a modest ferry as a controlled narrative anchor; lower nearer bank with more defined dry-brush rocks or sparse reeds/trees and darker accents that establish foreground weight—keep transitions continuous through bank shapes, mist, and brush rhythm rather than three disconnected bands. Place one or two tiny adult travelers in the ferry; keep them readable at gallery scale but clearly subordinate to landscape structure (no portrait close-up, no fashion-figure dominance). Prefer Southern Song lyrical mist and asymmetrical spatial breathing over Northern Song monumental mountain-filling masses. Build atmospheric recession through layered ink values, wet washes dissolving into void, and dry-brush texture on nearer rock and tree forms—not photographic depth of field, Gaussian blur, softbox lighting, or airbrush gradients. Use monochrome carbon ink on silk only. If Song selective living anchors mention robes, hair, or timber interiors, treat them only as optional minimal traveler notation for scale—or omit them—never as corridor fashion staging, architecture spectacle, or costume display. Do not invent calligraphy, seals, signatures, collector marks, dates, dynasty inscriptions, logos, or artist attribution. Do not introduce fantasy architecture, mythology, elaborate costume, modern fashion detail, foxing, cracks, or fake aging.

one or two tiny subordinate adult travelers in the ferry, readable but not portrait-dominant

director.moment: a quiet mid-crossing pause on still water under soft mist
director.action: the ferry drifts slowly between banks while landscape structure and void carry the painting
director.gaze: no portrait gaze; travelers are tiny ink notations without readable facial expression
director.body_weight: pictorial weight belongs to landforms and void; human marks are lightest subordinate accents
director.hand_logic: no hand close-ups; traveler gestures omitted or reduced to minimal ink tips
director.fabric_response: if robes appear, they are abbreviated ink shapes continuous with landscape grammar—not satin fashion physics and not Song corridor editorial wardrobe display
director.prop_interaction: boat is a small structural ink form on water-as-void; no second narrative props; no display furniture
director.foreground: nearer bank rocks/reeds/trees with denser dry-brush and texture strokes establishing lower-field weight
director.midground: ferry and open river void occupying substantial unpainted silk, continuous with upper mist and lower bank
director.background: distant hills dissolving into wet mist washes and reserved silk without monumental Northern Song mountain fill
director.camera: vertical hanging-scroll painting field, 4:5, painting surface edge-to-edge as the artwork itself; slight asymmetry allowed; not an eye-level fashion editorial frame and not a museum-object product shot
director.light_source: pictorial value from ink concentration and reserved silk only; no softbox, rim light, god-rays, cyclorama, or photographic beauty lighting
director.material_response: carbon ink on silk only: wet wash bloom and feathering into reserved silk for water/mist; dry-brush drag on nearer rock and tree; brush-tip taper; tonal hierarchy from untouched silk through pale gray wash to selective dark accents; silk weave may subtly affect stroke edges; do not render paper substrate behavior as the primary support; no acrylic impasto, no multicolor watercolor, no uniform airbrush gradient, no sepia filter, no photo-ink overlay
director.micro_story: distance between two shores felt through mist and unpainted water, with a ferry kept small enough that the landscape remains the subject
